answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every identity to solve a fresh cipher puzzle whose answer is cryptographically bound to that agent's public key before it may transact. Each solved puzzle mints a unique crystal token that peers attest on-chain; because the puzzle is keyed and non-transferable, one real identity cannot cheaply spawn many. An attacker who wants a swarm of fake agents must pay the full compute cost for each, so scaling sybils scales cost linearly. Unlike an ivory tower scheme that trusts self-declared IDs, this turns identity into provably scarce work.
